dataset_title: Continuous cattle-manure and grass co-digestion outcomes and digestate observations (abstract-level extract)
source_title: Co-digestion of cattle manure and grass harvested with different technologies. Effect on methane yield, digestate composition and energy balance
source_locations: Publisher abstract; study aim and abstract conclusions
data_basis: Minimal transcription of abstract-reported co-digestion conditions, relative methane outcomes, qualitative digestate findings, and relative energy statements. Reported comparisons and their denominators are retained as written; no absolute yield, energy demand, or nutrient concentration is inferred.
license: No reuse license for the full article was confirmed. This file contains a short factual abstract-level extract with attribution; no article tables, figures, or full text are reproduced.
applicability: Reference-only co-digestion comparator for Phases 3, 5, and 7. The study mixes natural grass with cattle manure, whereas GreenHub's main anaerobic-digestion route uses protein-recovery residuals. Its values do not calibrate the GreenHub residual stream.
limitations: Abstract-level only; no table-level raw data or replicate uncertainty were transcribed.
The grass co-feed is not GreenHub press cake, grass juice, post-protein residual, or roadside feed from the GreenHub supply chain.
The abstract does not give exact thermophilic temperature, absolute methane yield, methane flow, organic loading rate, operating duration, methane fraction baseline, or digestate concentrations.
The reported 6% decrease in methane concentration is not identified as a relative percent or percentage-point decrease; it is kept as reported and must not be converted.
The 14% mixing-energy comparison lacks a stated reactor-specific energy balance and is not a mixing-power coefficient.
No value is connected to the parameter registry, defaults, runtime calculations, UI, or Pareto scenarios.
curation_note: The DOI identifies the article. The local URN identifies this GreenHub transcription version and is not an externally registered persistent identifier.
